summary: REPAIRED block 1: P3 is WITHDRAWN. Propagating (2.6)-compactness up the paper's tower was my inference; it is false. Counterexample: the skew shift T(x,y)=(x+a,y+x) is (2.6)-compact over its rotation factor (q=1, zero error, coefficients e^{2 pi i k x}, modulus 1) and the rotation is compact over the point (eigenfunctions), yet the skew shift is not compact over the point: U_k(e^{2 pi i y}) = zeta_k e^{2 pi i k x} e^{2 pi i y} is an infinite orthonormal family, not approximable by any bounded-coefficient finite-rank module. So compact o compact != compact, even isometric o isometric. Second: there the paper's tower stops at the TOP factor (y1-y2 invariant on the relative product; successor generated by e^{2 pi i y} is all of X), so the tower does not force a proper terminal factor, and at Y=X the conclusion fails. H2 is NOT discharged. Missing lemma (M): terminal factor proper; sharpest form (M'''): a wild law is weakly mixing - then Lemma 2.4 suffices and Sec.2.4+Sec.3.1 go. Retained: Theorem A' (m5, machine-checked, H2 explicit), P2 (common-base joins), P1 for Haar only. Lean: m4's successor step is transitivity, refuted, so R1-R4 is unsound. Fallback: CENSUS twin pair. No builds, no search.
